task: NBA Physical Attributes Impact on Career Performance
summary: Both deliverables exist, are well-formed and complete; all reported statistics were independently recomputed from the three NBA CSVs with a clean re-implementation of the pipeline and match output.csv within 4-decimal rounding (max abs diff 5e-05).

independent_recomputation.method: Re-implemented the pipeline from source CSVs (filter player_id>0 -> dedup keep latest season -> inner join on person_id -> career_span=to_year-from_year+1 -> valid career 0..25 -> draft_round numeric in [1,10] -> height backfill from 'H-ft' -> scipy pearsonr pairwise-complete) and compared to output.csv.

png.layout: 2x2 (4 populated quadrants, each with non-trivial ink; titles band + per-panel axis labels detected)

panel_evidence.panel1_topleft_heatmap: heatmap + colorbar signature: RdBu colormap extremes/midtones present in the quadrant (colorbar gradient), dense ink area consistent with 4x2 annotated cell grid, x tick labels 'Draft Round'/'Career Span (yrs)'
panel_evidence.panel2_topright_bar: all four custom bar colors detected with pixel areas proportional to the weights (blue ~36%, green ~24%, orange ~1.7%, red ~38%)
panel_evidence.panel3_bottomleft_scatter_height_vs_draf: blue scatter points + dark-red least-squares line present; data n=571, height 67.75-86.0 in, draft round {1,2}, r=-0.1014 matches output
panel_evidence.panel4_bottomright_scatter_vertical_vs_c: green scatter points + dark-red least-squares line present; data n=585, vertical leap 25.0-44.0 in, career span 1-21 yrs, r=-0.0245 matches output

upstream_artifact_consistency.execute_summary.json: status=success; its key_intermediate_results.results_table and artifact list (output.csv, physical_attributes_analysis.png, analyze.py, execute_summary.json) agree with the files present and with the recomputed numbers.
upstream_artifact_consistency.analyze.py: Present (221 lines); implements exactly the documented pipeline, writes output.csv then physical_attributes_analysis.png from the same in-memory numbers.

observations_not_errors: Only height (r=-0.1014, p=0.0154) and 3/4 court sprint (r=+0.1236, p=0.0069) are significantly correlated with draft round; wingspan (p=0.099) and max vertical leap (p=0.700) are not.
No attribute has a significant correlation with career span (all p > 0.21), so the career half of the composite is weak evidence - the weights are dominated by the draft-round signal.

3/4 court sprint is inverted (lower = faster); its raw positive r vs draft round yields a negative composite (-0.1556), yet it receives the largest normalized weight (0.3770) because weights use |composite|. Max vertical leap is the only attribute with a negative composite and gets the minimum weight (0.0167).
Draft round is effectively binary (Round 1 = 337, Round 2 = 234) in the combine era, so the draft correlations are point-biserial on a restricted range.
Per-attribute pairwise n differs (477-691), so the normalized weights are not computed from an identical sample.
Round-to-round rounding: output.csv stores 4/6 decimals, so formula re-checks differ by <=1.2e-04 (pure representation artifact, not a computation error).
execute_summary.json notes matplotlib was unavailable in the system python and a throw-away venv at /tmp/venv was used; the PNG itself is valid regardless.
limitations: Survivorship/selection bias: athletic measurements exist only for combine invitees, and only 691 of 1175 unique invitees matched an NBA record.
Career span is right-censored for still-active players, attenuating the career correlations.
Univariate Pearson correlations do not control for position, entry age or era.
Independent verification repeats the same column choices as analyze.py, so it validates computation, not analytical judgement.
